**Twenty-fifth:** Allah's words ﴿Do you not like that Allah should forgive you?﴾ are an illustration and an argument: that is, just as you love Allah's pardon for your sins, so likewise you should forgive those beneath you. To this meaning the Prophet's words, peace be upon him, refer: "He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy."

**Twenty-sixth:** Some scholars said: This is the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah the Exalted, in terms of the gentleness of Allah toward the sinful slanderers through this expression. It was also said: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is His words: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty﴾ [al-Ahzab: 47]. And Allah said in another verse: ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds, in gardens of paradise, for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty﴾ [al-Shura: 22], so this verse explains the great bounty, and the other gives good tidings of it to the believers. Among the verses of hope is His words: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves..."﴾ [al-Zumar: 53], and His words: ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants﴾ [al-Shura: 19]. Some of them said: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha: 5], because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not be content while any one of his Ummah remained in the Fire.

**Twenty-seventh:** Allah's words ﴿that they should give﴾: that is, "an lā yu'tū" (that they should not give), so the "lā" was elided, like the saying of the speaker:

"Fa-qultu yamīnu Allāhi abraḥu qā'idan / wa-law qaṭaʿū ra'sī ladayka wa-awṣālī"

This is the first half of a line of Imru' al-Qays, whose completion is: "Or even if they cut off my head before you and my limbs."

Al-Zajjaj mentioned this. According to the view of Abu Ubayda, there is no need to suppose an elided "lā."

﴿And let them pardon﴾: from "afā al-rab'u," meaning it was effaced, so it is the erasure of the sin, just as the trace of the encampment is effaced.

**Twenty-eight issues** [It should be noted that the issues number twenty-seven in all the originals.]:

**First:** Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you﴾. "*ʿUsbah*" (a group, a band of men bound by mutual support) is the predicate of "*inna*". It is also permissible to put it in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*ḥāl*), in which case the predicate would be: "for every person among them is what he earned of sin."

The cause of its revelation is what the imams narrated from the lengthy *Ḥadīth al-Ifk* (the hadith of the slander, *al-ifk* meaning fabrication or lie) concerning the story of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her. It is a sound and well-known report, whose fame makes its mention unnecessary, and it will come in abridged form. Al-Bukhari transmitted it as a suspended report (*taʿlīq*), and his version is more complete. He said: "And Usamah said, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah." He also transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from his brother Sulayman, from the hadith of Masruq, from Umm Ruman, the mother of ʿĀʾishah, that she said: "When ʿĀʾishah was accused, she fell unconscious."

And from Musa ibn Isma'il, from the hadith of Abu Wa'il, who said: "Masruq ibn al-Ajda' related to me, he said: Umm Ruman, who is the mother of ʿĀʾishah, related to me, she said: While I and ʿĀʾishah were sitting, a woman of the Ansar entered and said: 'May Allah do such-and-such to so-and-so.' Umm Ruman said: 'And what is that?' She said: 'I am among those who spread the story!' She said: 'And what was that?' She said: 'Such-and-such.' ʿĀʾishah said: 'Did he hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' She said: 'Yes.' She said: 'And Abu Bakr?' She said: 'Yes!' So ʿĀʾishah fell unconscious, and she did not recover except with a fever accompanied by shivering [i.e., trembling]. I threw her clothes over her and covered her. The Prophet ﷺ came and said: 'What is the matter with this one?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a fever with shivering has seized her.' He said: 'Perhaps it is because of a report that has been spoken of.' She said: 'Yes.' Then ʿĀʾishah sat up and said: 'By Allah, if I swear an oath, you will not believe me! And if I offer an excuse, you will not accept my excuse! My example and yours is that of Jacob and his sons [i.e., when he said in his trial: "Allah is the One whose help is sought..." and so on], and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.' She said: 'He departed and said nothing, and Allah revealed her innocence.' She said: 'Praise be to Allah, not to anyone's praise, nor to yours.'"

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Humaydi said: "Some of the Baghdadi *ḥuffāẓ* (memorizers of hadith) whom we met used to say: the *irsāl* (a break in the chain) is clearer in this hadith, and they argued for this by the fact that Umm Ruman died during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Masruq did not witness the Prophet ﷺ, without any dispute."

Al-Bukhari also has, from the hadith of ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, that ʿĀʾishah used to recite ﴿when you received it with your tongues﴾ [24:15] and say: "*al-walq* is lying." Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: "She was more knowledgeable than others about that [i.e., about the reading she used], because it was revealed concerning her."

Al-Bukhari said: "Ma'mar [in al-Bukhari it is al-Nuʿmān ibn Rashid] ibn Rashid said, from al-Zuhri: The hadith of the slander occurred in the ghazwah (military campaign) of al-Muraysiʿ." Ibn Ishaq said: "And that was in the year six." Musa ibn ʿUqbah said: "In the year four."

Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: "al-Walid ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said to me: 'Has it reached you that ʿAli was among those who slandered?' I said: 'No, but two men of your people have informed me: Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman and Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, that ʿĀʾishah said to them both: "ʿAli was *musallaman* [silent] regarding her affair."'" [Note: *musallaman*, with a kasra on the *lām* and a shadda, from *tasliym*, meaning silent about her matter. It was also said: with a fatha on the *lām*, from safety from delving into it.]

Abu Bakr al-Ismaʿili transmitted it in his book *al-Mukhraj ʿalā al-Ṣaḥīḥ* by another route, from the hadith of Ma'mar from al-Zuhri, and in it: He said: "I was with al-Walid ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, and he said: 'The one who took on its greater part among them, is it ʿAli ibn Abi Talib?' I said: 'No. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, ʿUrwah, ʿAlqamah and ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtbah all related to me, all saying: I heard ʿĀʾishah say: "The one who took on its greater part was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy [ibn Salul]."'"

And al-Bukhari also transmitted from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah: "The one who took on its greater part among them was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy."

**Second:** Allah's saying ﴿with the slander﴾. *Al-ifk* is lying. *ʿUsbah* is three men, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, and it is also reported from him that it ranges from three to ten. Ibn ʿUyaynah said: forty men. Mujahid said: from ten to fifteen. Its root in language and in Arab speech is the group of people who support one another out of partisanship.

Good, in reality, is that whose benefit exceeds its harm; evil is that whose harm exceeds its benefit. Good with no evil in it is Paradise, and evil with no good in it is Hell. As for the affliction that descends upon the friends of Allah, it is good, because its harm, which is pain, is small in this world, and its good is the abundant reward in the Hereafter. So Allah alerted ʿĀʾishah, her household and Safwan, since the address is to them in His saying: ﴿Do not consider it bad for you; rather it is good for you﴾, because the benefit and good outweigh the side of evil.

**Third:** When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with ʿĀʾishah accompanying him in the ghazwah of Banu al-Mustaliq, which is the ghazwah of al-Muraysiʿ, and he turned back and drew near Medina, he announced the departure one night. She got up when they announced departure and walked until she passed beyond the army. When she had finished her business, she came back to the saddle and touched her chest, and found that a necklace of *jaza'* [a known bead, black with white streaks like veins] from Zafar [a city in Yemen] had broken. She returned and searched for it, and her search detained her. She found it and came back, but found no one there. She was a young woman, lightly fleshed, so the men lifted her howdah and did not perceive her absence from it. When she found no one, she lay down in her place, hoping that she would be missed and that they would come back for her. She fell asleep in that place, and nothing woke her except the words of Safwan ibn al-Muʿattal: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and to Him we return," because he had lagged behind the army to guard the baggage. It was also said that she woke at his *istirjaʿ* (saying "Indeed we belong to Allah..."), and he dismounted from his camel and stepped aside from her until ʿĀʾishah mounted, and he began leading her until he brought her to the army at the height of midday. Then the people of the slander fell into their talk.

The one around whom they gathered in it, and who sought it out, spread it, stirred it up and kindled it, was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the hypocrite. He was the one who saw Safwan holding the reins of ʿĀʾishah's camel, and he said: "By Allah, she has not escaped from him, nor has he escaped from her," and said: "The wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man." Among those who spoke this slander were Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah and Hamnah bint Jahsh.

This is an abridgement of the hadith. It is in its entirety and precision in al-Bukhari and Muslim, and it is more complete in Muslim.

When Safwan heard Hassan's words about the slander, he came and struck him on the head with a sword and said:

"Taste the edge of the sword on my behalf,
for I am a youth, when provoked, and not a poet."

A group seized Hassan, grabbed him by the collar [*labbaba*: to seize someone by the collar, i.e., to gather his garments at his chest and throat during a dispute and then drag him], and brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ waived the blood-claim for Hassan's wound and asked Safwan to pardon him for it. This indicates that Hassan was among those who took on the greater part, as will come, and Allah knows best.

Safwan was the companion in charge of the rear guard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his expeditions, because of his bravery, and he was among the best of the Companions [may Allah be pleased with him and with them]. It was said that he was *ḥaṣūr* (impotent), not approaching women; Ibn Ishaq mentioned this from the route of ʿĀʾishah. It was said that he had two sons. This is indicated by his hadith transmitted with his wife, and by the Prophet's ﷺ saying about his two sons: "They resemble him more than a crow resembles a crow." And his saying in the hadith: "By Allah, he never uncovered the covering of a woman," meaning fornication.

He was martyred, may Allah be pleased with him, in the ghazwah of Armenia in the year nineteen [AH], in the time of ʿUmar. It was also said: in the land of the Romans in the year fifty-eight, in the time of Muʿawiyah.

**Fourth:** Allah's saying ﴿For every person among them is what he earned of sin﴾, meaning from those who spoke the slander. None of the people of the slander were named except Hassan, Mistah, Hamnah and ʿAbd Allah; the rest remained unknown. This was said by ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, who was asked about it by ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and he said: "Except that they were a group, as Allah said."

In the *Muṣḥaf* (the written copy of the Qur'an) of Hafsah it reads: "*ʿUṣbah arbaʿah*" [a group of four]. [In k: "ʿuṣaybah", with the diminutive.]

**Fifth:** Allah's saying ﴿And the one who took on its greater part among them﴾. Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj and Yaʿqub read "*kubrahu*" with a *ḍamma* on the *kāf*. Al-Farrāʾ said: "This is a good reading, because the Arabs say: so-and-so took on the greater part [*ʿuẓm*] of such-and-such, i.e., its greatest part."

It is reported from ʿĀʾishah that he was Hassan, and she said when he became blind: "Perhaps the great punishment with which Allah threatened him is the loss of his sight," which Masruq narrated from her. It is also reported from her that he was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, and this is the sound report; Ibn ʿAbbas also said so.

Abu ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr related that ʿĀʾishah absolved Hassan of the false accusation and said: "He did not say anything." Hassan himself denied that he had said anything of that kind, in his verse:

"Chaste, steadfast, she is not suspected of any doubt,
and she wakes up hungry from the flesh of the heedless. [*Ḥaṣān*: chaste. *Razān*: steadfast, dignified, chaste. *Ghirthā*: hungry. *Mā tuzann*: is not suspected. *Al-ghawāfil*: plural of *ghāfilah*, i.e., she does not graze in people's honour.]

The beloved of the best of people in religion and lineage,
the Prophet of guidance and of noble and bountiful virtues.

The noblewoman of a tribe of Luʾayy ibn Ghālib,
of noble endeavours, whose glory never vanishes.

Refined, whom Allah has made good in her nature [*khīm*: nature, disposition, character, origin],
and purified from every blemish and falsehood.

If what has reached you is that I said it,
then let my fingers never lift my whip to me.

How then, when my love for her endures as long as I live, and my support
for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings?

She has a lofty rank over the people, whose excellence
the reach of the one who seeks to surpass falls short of."

It has been narrated that when he recited to her "Chaste, steadfast," she said to him: "You are not like that"; she meant that you fell into the heedless ones. This is a contradiction, and it can be reconciled by saying that Hassan did not say it explicitly and plainly; rather he made an allusion to it and hinted at it, so it was attributed to him. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 24, verses 11–22 (part 2 of 3):

Scholars have differed over whether he (ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy) engaged in the slander (al-ifk), and whether he received the prescribed punishment (al-hadd, the fixed penalty set by the Law). God knows best which of these was the case.

The sixth issue: Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) flogged two men and a woman for the slander: Mistah, Hassan and Hamnah. At-Tirmidhi also mentioned this. Al-Qushayri reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) flogged Ibn Ubayy eighty lashes, and for him in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire. Al-Qushayri said: What is established in the reports is that he struck Ibn Ubayy, and he struck Hassan and Hamnah. As for Mistah, no explicit slander has been established from him, but he used to listen and spread (the story) without explicit accusation.

Al-Mawardi [the seventh issue: al-Mawardi] and others said: They differed over whether the Prophet (ﷺ) inflicted the hadd on the people of the slander, and there are two views. One is that he did not inflict the hadd on any of the people of the slander, because the hadd punishments are only carried out on the basis of confession or proof, and God did not command him to carry them out on the basis of his report about them, just as He did not command him to kill the hypocrites, although He informed him of their disbelief. I say: This view is corrupt and contradicts the explicit text of the Qur'an, for God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses — lash them with eighty lashes﴾, meaning, as evidence for the truth of their claim. The second view: The Prophet (ﷺ) inflicted the hadd on the people of the slander: ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy, Mistah ibn Uthathah, Hassan ibn Thabit and Hamnah bint Jahsh. Concerning this a Muslim poet said:

Hassan has tasted what his people had,
and Hamnah, when they spoke foolishly, and Mistah.
And Ibn Salul tasted disgrace in the hadd,
as he plunged into a lie that speaks plainly.
They undertook to hurl baseless accusations at the wife of their Prophet,
and to provoke the wrath of the Lord of the Glorious Throne, so they went too far.
They harmed the Messenger of God in it, so they were lashed
with disgraces that remain; they were disgraced and exposed.
So there poured upon them stones [as if they were]
showers of rain pouring from the peaks of clouds.

I say: The well-known report and what is recognized among the scholars is that those who were given the hadd were Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah, and no hadd has been heard of for ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy. Abu Dawud narrated from ʿAisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: When my innocence was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) stood up, mentioned that, and recited the Qur'an. When he came down from the pulpit he ordered the two men and the woman, and they were struck their hadd, and he named them: Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah and Hamnah bint Jahsh. In the book of at-Tahawi (the text reads): "eighty, eighty." Our scholars said: ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy was not given the hadd because God, Exalted, had prepared for him a great punishment in the Hereafter; if he had been given the hadd in this world, that would have been a reduction of his punishment in the Hereafter and a lightening of it for him. Moreover, God, Exalted, has testified to the innocence of ʿAisha, may God be pleased with her, and to the lie of everyone who accused her, so the purpose of the hadd has been achieved, since its aim is to show the falsehood of the accuser and the innocence of the one accused, as God, Exalted, said: ﴿Then, since they did not bring witnesses, it is they who, in the sight of God, are the liars﴾. These believers were given the hadd only so that the sin of the slander they had committed would be expiated for them, so that no consequence of it would remain against them in the Hereafter. The Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning the hadd punishments: "They are an expiation for the one upon whom they are carried out", as in the hadith of ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit. It is also possible to say: The hadd of Ibn Ubayy was left out in order to win over his people, to respect his son, and to extinguish the blaze of the feared strife that could have followed from it, for its early signs had already appeared from Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah and his people, as in Sahih Muslim. And God knows best.

The seventh issue: God's saying: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think good of one another and say, "This is an obvious lie"?﴾ This is a rebuke from God, glorified and exalted, to the believers for their thinking when the people of the slander said what they said. Ibn Zayd said: The believers thought that a believer would not commit adultery with his own mother; this was related by al-Mahdawi. Here "lawla" (why not) means "halla" (why did they not). It was also said: The meaning is that the distinguished believing men and women should have judged the matter by their own selves, so that if such a thing seemed unlikely of them, it would be even more unlikely of ʿAisha and Safwan. It was reported that this sound reasoning occurred to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari and his wife. He entered upon her and she said to him: "O Abu Ayyub, have you heard what is being said?" He said: "Yes! And that is a lie! Would you, O Umm Ayyub, do such a thing?" She said: "No, by God!" He said: "Then ʿAisha, by God, is better than you." Umm Ayyub said: "Yes." This act and others like it is what God, Exalted, rebuked the believers for, since not all of them did it.

The eighth issue: God's saying ﴿by their own selves﴾. An-Nahhas said: The meaning of "by their own selves" is "by their brothers." So God made it obligatory upon the Muslims, when they hear a man slander someone and mention him with an ugliness that they do not know him to have, to deny it against him and to call him a liar, and He threatened those who abstain from doing so and those who transmit it.

I say: For this reason the scholars said: This verse is a foundation for the principle that the rank of faith which a person has attained, the status of righteousness which the believer has reached, and the garment of chastity with which the Muslim covers himself, are not removed from him by a report that is merely possible, even if it spreads, when its basis is corrupt or unknown.

The ninth issue: God's saying: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ This is a reproach to the people of the slander. "Lawla" here means "halla" (why did they not), i.e., why did they not bring four witnesses for what they alleged of the fabrication. This is a rejection of the first judgment and a referral to the earlier verse on slander.

The tenth issue: God's saying: ﴿Then, since they did not bring witnesses, it is they who, in the sight of God, are the liars﴾, meaning: they are liars in the judgment of God. A man may be unable to produce proof while being truthful in his accusation, yet in the judgment of the Law and the outward matter he is a liar, though not in the knowledge of God, Exalted. God only attached the hadd punishments to His ruling which He legislated in this world, not to the requirement of His knowledge which relates to the human being as he truly is. Thus the ruling of the Hereafter is what is built upon that.

I say: What strengthens this meaning and supports it is what al-Bukhari transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he said: "O people, revelation has ended, and we are now only holding you accountable for what has become apparent to us of your deeds. Whoever shows us good, we grant him security and bring him near, and we have no claim upon his inner intention; God will call him to account for his inner intention. Whoever shows us evil, we do not grant him security nor believe him, even if he says that his inner intention is good." The scholars unanimously agreed that the rulings of this world are based on what is outward, and that inner states are left to God, Mighty and Majestic.

The eleventh issue: God's saying: ﴿And if not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy...﴾ [This refers to verse 10, which is God's saying: "And if not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy, and that God is Forgiving and Wise."] The word "fadl" (bounty) is in the nominative case as the subject (mubtada') according to Sibawayh, and the predicate is omitted, which the Arabs do not make explicit. The answer to "lawla" is omitted because a similar one was mentioned afterwards. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And if not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy, [it would have] touched you...﴾, meaning: because of what you said about ʿAisha, a great punishment in this world and the Hereafter would have struck you. This is an eloquent rebuke from God, yet with His mercy He concealed it for you in this world, and He will show mercy in the Hereafter to whoever comes to Him in repentance. "Al-ifada" means: taking up in the talk, and it is this that the rebuke fell upon. It is said: "The people plunged into the talk" (afada al-qawm fi'l-hadith), meaning they took up in it.

The twelfth issue: God's saying: ﴿When you received it with your tongues﴾. The reading of Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqaʿ is with a damma on the first letter of "tatalaqqawnahu," a sukun on the lam, and a damma on the qaf, from "al-ilqa'" (casting), and this is a clear reading. Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud read "idh tatalaqqawnahu" from "al-talaqqi," with two taʾs. The majority of the Seven read with one taʾ and clear pronunciation of the dhal without idgham (assimilation), and this too is from "al-talaqqi." Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read with idgham of the dhal into the taʾ. Ibn Kathir read with the dhal clearly pronounced and the taʾ assimilated into the taʾ, and this is an uneasy reading, because it requires two consecutive sukuns; it is not like the assimilation in the reading of the one who reads "fala tanajaw. Wa la tanabazu" (Do not confide in one another, nor insult one another by nicknames), because there the alif, a silent letter, intervenes, and since it is a soft vowel letter, that was acceptable there, which is not acceptable with a sukun on the dhal. Ibn Yaʿmur and ʿAisha, may God be pleased with them both, who are the most knowledgeable people in this matter, read "idh talaqqunahu" with a fatha on the taʾ, a kasra on the lam and a damma on the qaf. The meaning of this reading comes from the Arab saying: "Waqa al-rajul yalqu waqlan" when he lied and persisted in it, so they used the transitive verb as evidence for the intransitive. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: In my view, he meant "idh talaqqunahu fihi" (when you were lying about it), so the preposition was omitted and the pronoun attached. Al-Khalil and Abu ʿAmr said: The origin of "al-walq" is haste; it is said: "The camels came hastening" (jaʾat al-ibilu talaq), i.e., they hastened. He said:

When they saw an army upon them that had come by night,
they came with flocks from al-Sham, hastening.
Indeed al-Husayn is slippery and quick to climax,
she brought him, a strong she-camel from al-Sham, hastening.

It is said: "a man who is zalaq and zumlaq," on the pattern of "hudabid," and "zumalaq" and "zumlaq" (with a shadda on the mim), which is one who ejaculates before he has intercourse. The rajaz poet said:

Indeed al-Husayn is zalaq and zumlaq.

Al-walq also means light stabbing. One says "walaqahu yalquhu walqan." It is said: "walaqahu bi'l-sayf walaqat," i.e., blows, so the word is homonymous.

The thirteenth issue: God's saying: ﴿And you say with your mouths﴾, which is intensification, obligation and emphasis. The pronoun in "tahsabunahu" (you consider it) refers to the speech, plunging into it, and spreading it. "Hayyinan" means: slight and easy, not reaching you with any sin.

﴿And it is, in the sight of God, grave﴾, in respect of the burden. This is like his saying (ﷺ) in the hadith of the two graves: "Indeed they are being punished, and they are not being punished for something great", meaning in relation to you.

**Fourteenth:** Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander"? Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it again, if you are believers. And Allah makes the signs clear to you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ This is a rebuke addressed to all the believers. The meaning is: it was incumbent upon you to disapprove of it, and that none of you should take it up and pass it on from one to another by way of relating and transmitting it. You should also have declared Allah exalted above such a thing occurring from the wife of His Prophet, peace be upon him. And you should have judged this statement to be a slander (buhtan). The reality of buhtan is saying about a person what is not in him, whereas ghiba (backbiting) is saying about a person what is in him. This meaning has been reported in the authentic hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Then Allah admonished them against returning to a similar situation. The word "an" (that) is a object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi), with the implied sense of "out of dislike that," or the like.

**Fifteenth:** Allah's words ﴿if you are believers﴾ are a reminder and an emphasis, just as you would say, "It is fitting for you to do such and such, if you are a man."

**Sixteenth:** Allah's words ﴿Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it﴾ refer to Aisha, because "the like of it" can only be a parallel of the accusation concerning the very same person, or concerning one of the same rank as her among the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). This is because such an act harms the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his honour and his family, and that is disbelief (kufr) on the part of the one who does it.

**Seventeenth:** Hisham ibn Ammar said: I heard Malik say, "Whoever insults Abu Bakr and Umar is to be disciplined, and whoever insults Aisha is to be put to death, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it, if you are believers﴾. So whoever insults Aisha has opposed the Qur'an, and whoever opposes the Qur'an is put to death."

Ibn al-Arabi said: The companions of al-Shafi'i said, "Whoever insults Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, is to be disciplined as is done for the rest of the believers. And the words ﴿if you are believers﴾ were not said concerning Aisha, because that [i.e., insulting her] would be disbelief. Rather, it is as he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man does not believe whose neighbour is not safe from his evils.'" And if removing faith in the one who insults Aisha were literal, then removing faith in the statement "An adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer" would also be literal.

We reply: It is not as you claim. Rather, the People of the Slander (ahl al-ifk) accused Aisha, the pure one, of indecency, and Allah cleared her. So everyone who insults her with that of which Allah has cleared her is one who denies Allah, and whoever denies Allah is a disbeliever. This is the path of Malik's position, and it is a clear way for people of insight. And if a man insulted Aisha with something other than that from which Allah cleared her, his punishment would be discipline.

**Eighteenth:** Allah's words ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe﴾: that is, that it should spread and become widely known. It is said: "shā'a al-shay'u shuyū'an, wa-shi'an, wa-shi'ānan, wa-shuyū'uh," meaning it became apparent and spread.

﴿Among those who believe﴾: that is, among the chaste men and the chaste women. By this general expression what is meant is Aisha and Safwan, may Allah be pleased with them both. "Al-fāḥisha" (indecency) is an act that is ugly to an extreme degree. It is also said that "al-fāḥisha" in this verse means an evil statement.

﴿For them is a painful punishment in this world﴾: that is, the prescribed punishment (hadd). ﴿And in the Hereafter, the punishment of the Fire﴾: that is, for the hypocrites, so this is specific. We have already explained that the hadd is an expiation (kaffara) for believers. al-Tabari said: its meaning is, if he dies persisting in it without repenting.

**Nineteenth:** Allah's words ﴿And Allah knows﴾: that is, He knows the magnitude of this sin and the recompense for it, and He knows everything.

﴿And you do not know﴾: it has been narrated from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever supports a man among the people in a dispute about which he has no knowledge, he is in the wrath of Allah until he desists from it. And whoever intercedes on behalf of someone so that a prescribed punishment from the punishments of Allah is not carried out, he has truly defied Allah and brought upon himself His wrath, and the curse of Allah follows him until the Day of Resurrection. And whoever spreads a word against a Muslim man, while he is innocent of it, intending to disgrace him with it in this world, it is incumbent upon Allah to cast him into the Fire with it." Then he recited as its confirmation from the Book of Allah: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe﴾, the verse.

**Twentieth:** Allah's words ﴿O you who have believed, do not follow the steps of Satan﴾: that is, his paths and ways. The meaning: do not travel the road to which Satan calls you. The singular of "khuṭuwāt" is "khuṭwa," which is the distance between the two feet. "Al-khaṭwa" (with a fatḥa) is the verbal noun: one says "khaṭawtu khaṭwatan," and its plural is "khaṭawāt." And "takhaṭṭā ilaynā fulān" (so-and-so stepped over to us), and from this is the hadith that he saw a man stepping over the necks of people on Friday.

The majority of readers recited "khuṭuwāt" with a ḍamma on the ṭā'. ʿĀṣim and al-A'mash read it with sukūn. The majority read "mā zakā" with a light kāf, meaning he was not guided, nor did he accept Islam, nor did he recognise right guidance. It is also said that "mā zakā" means he did not become righteous; one says "zakā yazkū zakā'an," meaning he became righteous. Al-Hasan and Abu Ḥaywa read it with a shaddah, meaning that His purifying you, His cleansing of you and His guidance of you come only through His grace, not through your deeds.

Al-Kisa'i said: "Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū lā tattabiʿū khuṭuwāti al-shayṭān" is a parenthetical clause (mu'taridh), and His words "mā zakā minkum min aḥadin abadan" (none of you would ever have been purified) are the answer to His earlier and second statement: ﴿And if not for the grace of Allah upon you﴾.

**Twenty-first:** Allah's words ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give﴾, the verse. The most well-known of the reports is that this verse was revealed concerning the story of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa, may Allah be pleased with him, and Mistah ibn Uthatha. That was because Mistah was the son of his maternal aunt's daughter, and he was among the poor Emigrants and the Badr veterans. He is Mistah ibn Uthatha ibn ʿAbbad ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manaf. It is also said that his name was Awf, and Mistah was a nickname. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, used to spend on him because of his poverty and kinship. When the matter of the slander occurred, and Mistah said what he said, Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend on him nor benefit him with any benefit ever. Then Mistah came and made excuses, saying: "I was only frequenting the gatherings of Hassan, and I would listen but not speak." Abu Bakr said to him: "You laughed and took part in what was said." And he passed by his right side (i.e., he swore an oath), and then the verse was revealed.

Al-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas said: A group of the believers cut off their benefits from everyone who spoke about the slander, and they said: "By Allah, we will not maintain relations with anyone who spoke about the matter of Aisha." So the verse was revealed concerning all of them.

The first (the report about Abu Bakr and Mistah) is more sound. However, the verse includes the Ummah until the Day of Resurrection, in that no one of virtue and wealth should become angry and swear that he will never benefit one who has such a description.

In the authentic report: when Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you﴾, the ten verses, Abu Bakr, who had been spending on Mistah because of his kinship and poverty, said: "By Allah, I will never spend anything on him again after what he said about Aisha." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give﴾, up to His words: ﴿Do you not like that Allah should forgive you?﴾. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: This is the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah the Exalted. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, I truly love that Allah should forgive me." So he returned to Mistah the provision he used to spend on him and said: "I will never withdraw it from him."

**Twenty-second:** In this verse there is evidence that slander (qadhf), even if it is a major sin, does not nullify good deeds, because Allah the Exalted described Mistah after his statement with emigration and faith. The same applies to all the major sins. Nothing nullifies deeds except associating partners with Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65].

**Twenty-third:** Whoever swears an oath not to do something, then sees that doing it is better, should do it and make expiation (kaffara) for his oath, or make expiation for his oath and then do it, as has preceded in Surat al-Ma'ida. The jurists held that whoever swears never to do a sunnah (a recommended practice) or a mandub (commendable act), and makes that permanent, this is a disqualification (jarh) of his testimony. Al-Baji mentioned this in al-Muntaqa.

**Twenty-fourth:** Allah's words ﴿And let not those of virtue﴾: "wa-lā ya'tali" means he swears, its pattern is yaf'ali, from al-alliyya, which is the oath, and from it is the Exalted's words ﴿for those who swear off from their wives﴾ (al-Baqara: 226), which has already been discussed in Surat al-Baqara. A group said its meaning is "yuqassir" (falls short), from your saying "alawtu fī kadhā" when you fell short in it, and from it is the Exalted's words ﴿they do not fall short in harming you﴾ (Ali 'Imran: 118).

**Twenty-fifth:** Allah's words ﴿Do you not like that Allah should forgive you?﴾ are an illustration and an argument: that is, just as you love Allah's pardon for your sins, so likewise you should forgive those beneath you. To this meaning the Prophet's words, peace be upon him, refer: "He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy."

**Twenty-sixth:** Some scholars said: This is the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah the Exalted, in terms of the gentleness of Allah toward the sinful slanderers through this expression. It was also said: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is His words: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty﴾ [al-Ahzab: 47]. And Allah said in another verse: ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds, in gardens of paradise, for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty﴾ [al-Shura: 22], so this verse explains the great bounty, and the other gives good tidings of it to the believers. Among the verses of hope is His words: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves..."﴾ [al-Zumar: 53], and His words: ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants﴾ [al-Shura: 19]. Some of them said: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha: 5], because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not be content while any one of his Ummah remained in the Fire.

**Twenty-seventh:** Allah's words ﴿that they should give﴾: that is, "an lā yu'tū" (that they should not give), so the "lā" was elided, like the saying of the speaker:

"Fa-qultu yamīnu Allāhi abraḥu qā'idan / wa-law qaṭaʿū ra'sī ladayka wa-awṣālī"

This is the first half of a line of Imru' al-Qays, whose completion is: "Or even if they cut off my head before you and my limbs."

Al-Zajjaj mentioned this. According to the view of Abu Ubayda, there is no need to suppose an elided "lā."

﴿And let them pardon﴾: from "afā al-rab'u," meaning it was effaced, so it is the erasure of the sin, just as the trace of the encampment is effaced.

**Twenty-eight issues** [It should be noted that the issues number twenty-seven in all the originals.]:

**First:** Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you﴾. "*ʿUsbah*" (a group, a band of men bound by mutual support) is the predicate of "*inna*". It is also permissible to put it in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*ḥāl*), in which case the predicate would be: "for every person among them is what he earned of sin."

The cause of its revelation is what the imams narrated from the lengthy *Ḥadīth al-Ifk* (the hadith of the slander, *al-ifk* meaning fabrication or lie) concerning the story of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her. It is a sound and well-known report, whose fame makes its mention unnecessary, and it will come in abridged form. Al-Bukhari transmitted it as a suspended report (*taʿlīq*), and his version is more complete. He said: "And Usamah said, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah." He also transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from his brother Sulayman, from the hadith of Masruq, from Umm Ruman, the mother of ʿĀʾishah, that she said: "When ʿĀʾishah was accused, she fell unconscious."

And from Musa ibn Isma'il, from the hadith of Abu Wa'il, who said: "Masruq ibn al-Ajda' related to me, he said: Umm Ruman, who is the mother of ʿĀʾishah, related to me, she said: While I and ʿĀʾishah were sitting, a woman of the Ansar entered and said: 'May Allah do such-and-such to so-and-so.' Umm Ruman said: 'And what is that?' She said: 'I am among those who spread the story!' She said: 'And what was that?' She said: 'Such-and-such.' ʿĀʾishah said: 'Did he hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' She said: 'Yes.' She said: 'And Abu Bakr?' She said: 'Yes!' So ʿĀʾishah fell unconscious, and she did not recover except with a fever accompanied by shivering [i.e., trembling]. I threw her clothes over her and covered her. The Prophet ﷺ came and said: 'What is the matter with this one?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a fever with shivering has seized her.' He said: 'Perhaps it is because of a report that has been spoken of.' She said: 'Yes.' Then ʿĀʾishah sat up and said: 'By Allah, if I swear an oath, you will not believe me! And if I offer an excuse, you will not accept my excuse! My example and yours is that of Jacob and his sons [i.e., when he said in his trial: "Allah is the One whose help is sought..." and so on], and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.' She said: 'He departed and said nothing, and Allah revealed her innocence.' She said: 'Praise be to Allah, not to anyone's praise, nor to yours.'"

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Humaydi said: "Some of the Baghdadi *ḥuffāẓ* (memorizers of hadith) whom we met used to say: the *irsāl* (a break in the chain) is clearer in this hadith, and they argued for this by the fact that Umm Ruman died during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Masruq did not witness the Prophet ﷺ, without any dispute."

Al-Bukhari also has, from the hadith of ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, that ʿĀʾishah used to recite ﴿when you received it with your tongues﴾ [24:15] and say: "*al-walq* is lying." Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: "She was more knowledgeable than others about that [i.e., about the reading she used], because it was revealed concerning her."

Al-Bukhari said: "Ma'mar [in al-Bukhari it is al-Nuʿmān ibn Rashid] ibn Rashid said, from al-Zuhri: The hadith of the slander occurred in the ghazwah (military campaign) of al-Muraysiʿ." Ibn Ishaq said: "And that was in the year six." Musa ibn ʿUqbah said: "In the year four."

Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: "al-Walid ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said to me: 'Has it reached you that ʿAli was among those who slandered?' I said: 'No, but two men of your people have informed me: Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman and Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, that ʿĀʾishah said to them both: "ʿAli was *musallaman* [silent] regarding her affair."'" [Note: *musallaman*, with a kasra on the *lām* and a shadda, from *tasliym*, meaning silent about her matter. It was also said: with a fatha on the *lām*, from safety from delving into it.]

Abu Bakr al-Ismaʿili transmitted it in his book *al-Mukhraj ʿalā al-Ṣaḥīḥ* by another route, from the hadith of Ma'mar from al-Zuhri, and in it: He said: "I was with al-Walid ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, and he said: 'The one who took on its greater part among them, is it ʿAli ibn Abi Talib?' I said: 'No. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, ʿUrwah, ʿAlqamah and ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtbah all related to me, all saying: I heard ʿĀʾishah say: "The one who took on its greater part was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy [ibn Salul]."'"

And al-Bukhari also transmitted from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah: "The one who took on its greater part among them was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy."

**Second:** Allah's saying ﴿with the slander﴾. *Al-ifk* is lying. *ʿUsbah* is three men, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, and it is also reported from him that it ranges from three to ten. Ibn ʿUyaynah said: forty men. Mujahid said: from ten to fifteen. Its root in language and in Arab speech is the group of people who support one another out of partisanship.

Good, in reality, is that whose benefit exceeds its harm; evil is that whose harm exceeds its benefit. Good with no evil in it is Paradise, and evil with no good in it is Hell. As for the affliction that descends upon the friends of Allah, it is good, because its harm, which is pain, is small in this world, and its good is the abundant reward in the Hereafter. So Allah alerted ʿĀʾishah, her household and Safwan, since the address is to them in His saying: ﴿Do not consider it bad for you; rather it is good for you﴾, because the benefit and good outweigh the side of evil.

**Third:** When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with ʿĀʾishah accompanying him in the ghazwah of Banu al-Mustaliq, which is the ghazwah of al-Muraysiʿ, and he turned back and drew near Medina, he announced the departure one night. She got up when they announced departure and walked until she passed beyond the army. When she had finished her business, she came back to the saddle and touched her chest, and found that a necklace of *jaza'* [a known bead, black with white streaks like veins] from Zafar [a city in Yemen] had broken. She returned and searched for it, and her search detained her. She found it and came back, but found no one there. She was a young woman, lightly fleshed, so the men lifted her howdah and did not perceive her absence from it. When she found no one, she lay down in her place, hoping that she would be missed and that they would come back for her. She fell asleep in that place, and nothing woke her except the words of Safwan ibn al-Muʿattal: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and to Him we return," because he had lagged behind the army to guard the baggage. It was also said that she woke at his *istirjaʿ* (saying "Indeed we belong to Allah..."), and he dismounted from his camel and stepped aside from her until ʿĀʾishah mounted, and he began leading her until he brought her to the army at the height of midday. Then the people of the slander fell into their talk.

The one around whom they gathered in it, and who sought it out, spread it, stirred it up and kindled it, was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the hypocrite. He was the one who saw Safwan holding the reins of ʿĀʾishah's camel, and he said: "By Allah, she has not escaped from him, nor has he escaped from her," and said: "The wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man." Among those who spoke this slander were Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah and Hamnah bint Jahsh.

This is an abridgement of the hadith. It is in its entirety and precision in al-Bukhari and Muslim, and it is more complete in Muslim.

When Safwan heard Hassan's words about the slander, he came and struck him on the head with a sword and said:

"Taste the edge of the sword on my behalf,
for I am a youth, when provoked, and not a poet."

A group seized Hassan, grabbed him by the collar [*labbaba*: to seize someone by the collar, i.e., to gather his garments at his chest and throat during a dispute and then drag him], and brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ waived the blood-claim for Hassan's wound and asked Safwan to pardon him for it. This indicates that Hassan was among those who took on the greater part, as will come, and Allah knows best.

Safwan was the companion in charge of the rear guard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his expeditions, because of his bravery, and he was among the best of the Companions [may Allah be pleased with him and with them]. It was said that he was *ḥaṣūr* (impotent), not approaching women; Ibn Ishaq mentioned this from the route of ʿĀʾishah. It was said that he had two sons. This is indicated by his hadith transmitted with his wife, and by the Prophet's ﷺ saying about his two sons: "They resemble him more than a crow resembles a crow." And his saying in the hadith: "By Allah, he never uncovered the covering of a woman," meaning fornication.

He was martyred, may Allah be pleased with him, in the ghazwah of Armenia in the year nineteen [AH], in the time of ʿUmar. It was also said: in the land of the Romans in the year fifty-eight, in the time of Muʿawiyah.

**Fourth:** Allah's saying ﴿For every person among them is what he earned of sin﴾, meaning from those who spoke the slander. None of the people of the slander were named except Hassan, Mistah, Hamnah and ʿAbd Allah; the rest remained unknown. This was said by ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, who was asked about it by ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and he said: "Except that they were a group, as Allah said."

In the *Muṣḥaf* (the written copy of the Qur'an) of Hafsah it reads: "*ʿUṣbah arbaʿah*" [a group of four]. [In k: "ʿuṣaybah", with the diminutive.]

**Fifth:** Allah's saying ﴿And the one who took on its greater part among them﴾. Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj and Yaʿqub read "*kubrahu*" with a *ḍamma* on the *kāf*. Al-Farrāʾ said: "This is a good reading, because the Arabs say: so-and-so took on the greater part [*ʿuẓm*] of such-and-such, i.e., its greatest part."

It is reported from ʿĀʾishah that he was Hassan, and she said when he became blind: "Perhaps the great punishment with which Allah threatened him is the loss of his sight," which Masruq narrated from her. It is also reported from her that he was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, and this is the sound report; Ibn ʿAbbas also said so.

Abu ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr related that ʿĀʾishah absolved Hassan of the false accusation and said: "He did not say anything." Hassan himself denied that he had said anything of that kind, in his verse:

"Chaste, steadfast, she is not suspected of any doubt,
and she wakes up hungry from the flesh of the heedless. [*Ḥaṣān*: chaste. *Razān*: steadfast, dignified, chaste. *Ghirthā*: hungry. *Mā tuzann*: is not suspected. *Al-ghawāfil*: plural of *ghāfilah*, i.e., she does not graze in people's honour.]

The beloved of the best of people in religion and lineage,
the Prophet of guidance and of noble and bountiful virtues.

The noblewoman of a tribe of Luʾayy ibn Ghālib,
of noble endeavours, whose glory never vanishes.

Refined, whom Allah has made good in her nature [*khīm*: nature, disposition, character, origin],
and purified from every blemish and falsehood.

If what has reached you is that I said it,
then let my fingers never lift my whip to me.

How then, when my love for her endures as long as I live, and my support
for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings?

She has a lofty rank over the people, whose excellence
the reach of the one who seeks to surpass falls short of."

It has been narrated that when he recited to her "Chaste, steadfast," she said to him: "You are not like that"; she meant that you fell into the heedless ones. This is a contradiction, and it can be reconciled by saying that Hassan did not say it explicitly and plainly; rather he made an allusion to it and hinted at it, so it was attributed to him. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 24, verses 11–22 (part 2 of 3):

Scholars have differed over whether he (ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy) engaged in the slander (al-ifk), and whether he received the prescribed punishment (al-hadd, the fixed penalty set by the Law). God knows best which of these was the case.

The sixth issue: Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) flogged two men and a woman for the slander: Mistah, Hassan and Hamnah. At-Tirmidhi also mentioned this. Al-Qushayri reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) flogged Ibn Ubayy eighty lashes, and for him in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire. Al-Qushayri said: What is established in the reports is that he struck Ibn Ubayy, and he struck Hassan and Hamnah. As for Mistah, no explicit slander has been established from him, but he used to listen and spread (the story) without explicit accusation.

Al-Mawardi [the seventh issue: al-Mawardi] and others said: They differed over whether the Prophet (ﷺ) inflicted the hadd on the people of the slander, and there are two views. One is that he did not inflict the hadd on any of the people of the slander, because the hadd punishments are only carried out on the basis of confession or proof, and God did not command him to carry them out on the basis of his report about them, just as He did not command him to kill the hypocrites, although He informed him of their disbelief. I say: This view is corrupt and contradicts the explicit text of the Qur'an, for God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses — lash them with eighty lashes﴾, meaning, as evidence for the truth of their claim. The second view: The Prophet (ﷺ) inflicted the hadd on the people of the slander: ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy, Mistah ibn Uthathah, Hassan ibn Thabit and Hamnah bint Jahsh. Concerning this a Muslim poet said:

Hassan has tasted what his people had,
and Hamnah, when they spoke foolishly, and Mistah.
And Ibn Salul tasted disgrace in the hadd,
as he plunged into a lie that speaks plainly.
They undertook to hurl baseless accusations at the wife of their Prophet,
and to provoke the wrath of the Lord of the Glorious Throne, so they went too far.
They harmed the Messenger of God in it, so they were lashed
with disgraces that remain; they were disgraced and exposed.
So there poured upon them stones [as if they were]
showers of rain pouring from the peaks of clouds.

I say: The well-known report and what is recognized among the scholars is that those who were given the hadd were Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah, and no hadd has been heard of for ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy. Abu Dawud narrated from ʿAisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: When my innocence was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) stood up, mentioned that, and recited the Qur'an. When he came down from the pulpit he ordered the two men and the woman, and they were struck their hadd, and he named them: Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah and Hamnah bint Jahsh. In the book of at-Tahawi (the text reads): "eighty, eighty." Our scholars said: ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy was not given the hadd because God, Exalted, had prepared for him a great punishment in the Hereafter; if he had been given the hadd in this world, that would have been a reduction of his punishment in the Hereafter and a lightening of it for him. Moreover, God, Exalted, has testified to the innocence of ʿAisha, may God be pleased with her, and to the lie of everyone who accused her, so the purpose of the hadd has been achieved, since its aim is to show the falsehood of the accuser and the innocence of the one accused, as God, Exalted, said: ﴿Then, since they did not bring witnesses, it is they who, in the sight of God, are the liars﴾. These believers were given the hadd only so that the sin of the slander they had committed would be expiated for them, so that no consequence of it would remain against them in the Hereafter. The Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning the hadd punishments: "They are an expiation for the one upon whom they are carried out", as in the hadith of ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit. It is also possible to say: The hadd of Ibn Ubayy was left out in order to win over his people, to respect his son, and to extinguish the blaze of the feared strife that could have followed from it, for its early signs had already appeared from Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah and his people, as in Sahih Muslim. And God knows best.

The seventh issue: God's saying: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think good of one another and say, "This is an obvious lie"?﴾ This is a rebuke from God, glorified and exalted, to the believers for their thinking when the people of the slander said what they said. Ibn Zayd said: The believers thought that a believer would not commit adultery with his own mother; this was related by al-Mahdawi. Here "lawla" (why not) means "halla" (why did they not). It was also said: The meaning is that the distinguished believing men and women should have judged the matter by their own selves, so that if such a thing seemed unlikely of them, it would be even more unlikely of ʿAisha and Safwan. It was reported that this sound reasoning occurred to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari and his wife. He entered upon her and she said to him: "O Abu Ayyub, have you heard what is being said?" He said: "Yes! And that is a lie! Would you, O Umm Ayyub, do such a thing?" She said: "No, by God!" He said: "Then ʿAisha, by God, is better than you." Umm Ayyub said: "Yes." This act and others like it is what God, Exalted, rebuked the believers for, since not all of them did it.

The eighth issue: God's saying ﴿by their own selves﴾. An-Nahhas said: The meaning of "by their own selves" is "by their brothers." So God made it obligatory upon the Muslims, when they hear a man slander someone and mention him with an ugliness that they do not know him to have, to deny it against him and to call him a liar, and He threatened those who abstain from doing so and those who transmit it.

I say: For this reason the scholars said: This verse is a foundation for the principle that the rank of faith which a person has attained, the status of righteousness which the believer has reached, and the garment of chastity with which the Muslim covers himself, are not removed from him by a report that is merely possible, even if it spreads, when its basis is corrupt or unknown.

The ninth issue: God's saying: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ This is a reproach to the people of the slander. "Lawla" here means "halla" (why did they not), i.e., why did they not bring four witnesses for what they alleged of the fabrication. This is a rejection of the first judgment and a referral to the earlier verse on slander.

The tenth issue: God's saying: ﴿Then, since they did not bring witnesses, it is they who, in the sight of God, are the liars﴾, meaning: they are liars in the judgment of God. A man may be unable to produce proof while being truthful in his accusation, yet in the judgment of the Law and the outward matter he is a liar, though not in the knowledge of God, Exalted. God only attached the hadd punishments to His ruling which He legislated in this world, not to the requirement of His knowledge which relates to the human being as he truly is. Thus the ruling of the Hereafter is what is built upon that.

I say: What strengthens this meaning and supports it is what al-Bukhari transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he said: "O people, revelation has ended, and we are now only holding you accountable for what has become apparent to us of your deeds. Whoever shows us good, we grant him security and bring him near, and we have no claim upon his inner intention; God will call him to account for his inner intention. Whoever shows us evil, we do not grant him security nor believe him, even if he says that his inner intention is good." The scholars unanimously agreed that the rulings of this world are based on what is outward, and that inner states are left to God, Mighty and Majestic.

The eleventh issue: God's saying: ﴿And if not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy...﴾ [This refers to verse 10, which is God's saying: "And if not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy, and that God is Forgiving and Wise."] The word "fadl" (bounty) is in the nominative case as the subject (mubtada') according to Sibawayh, and the predicate is omitted, which the Arabs do not make explicit. The answer to "lawla" is omitted because a similar one was mentioned afterwards. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And if not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy, [it would have] touched you...﴾, meaning: because of what you said about ʿAisha, a great punishment in this world and the Hereafter would have struck you. This is an eloquent rebuke from God, yet with His mercy He concealed it for you in this world, and He will show mercy in the Hereafter to whoever comes to Him in repentance. "Al-ifada" means: taking up in the talk, and it is this that the rebuke fell upon. It is said: "The people plunged into the talk" (afada al-qawm fi'l-hadith), meaning they took up in it.

The twelfth issue: God's saying: ﴿When you received it with your tongues﴾. The reading of Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqaʿ is with a damma on the first letter of "tatalaqqawnahu," a sukun on the lam, and a damma on the qaf, from "al-ilqa'" (casting), and this is a clear reading. Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud read "idh tatalaqqawnahu" from "al-talaqqi," with two taʾs. The majority of the Seven read with one taʾ and clear pronunciation of the dhal without idgham (assimilation), and this too is from "al-talaqqi." Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read with idgham of the dhal into the taʾ. Ibn Kathir read with the dhal clearly pronounced and the taʾ assimilated into the taʾ, and this is an uneasy reading, because it requires two consecutive sukuns; it is not like the assimilation in the reading of the one who reads "fala tanajaw. Wa la tanabazu" (Do not confide in one another, nor insult one another by nicknames), because there the alif, a silent letter, intervenes, and since it is a soft vowel letter, that was acceptable there, which is not acceptable with a sukun on the dhal. Ibn Yaʿmur and ʿAisha, may God be pleased with them both, who are the most knowledgeable people in this matter, read "idh talaqqunahu" with a fatha on the taʾ, a kasra on the lam and a damma on the qaf. The meaning of this reading comes from the Arab saying: "Waqa al-rajul yalqu waqlan" when he lied and persisted in it, so they used the transitive verb as evidence for the intransitive. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: In my view, he meant "idh talaqqunahu fihi" (when you were lying about it), so the preposition was omitted and the pronoun attached. Al-Khalil and Abu ʿAmr said: The origin of "al-walq" is haste; it is said: "The camels came hastening" (jaʾat al-ibilu talaq), i.e., they hastened. He said:

When they saw an army upon them that had come by night,
they came with flocks from al-Sham, hastening.
Indeed al-Husayn is slippery and quick to climax,
she brought him, a strong she-camel from al-Sham, hastening.

It is said: "a man who is zalaq and zumlaq," on the pattern of "hudabid," and "zumalaq" and "zumlaq" (with a shadda on the mim), which is one who ejaculates before he has intercourse. The rajaz poet said:

Indeed al-Husayn is zalaq and zumlaq.

Al-walq also means light stabbing. One says "walaqahu yalquhu walqan." It is said: "walaqahu bi'l-sayf walaqat," i.e., blows, so the word is homonymous.

The thirteenth issue: God's saying: ﴿And you say with your mouths﴾, which is intensification, obligation and emphasis. The pronoun in "tahsabunahu" (you consider it) refers to the speech, plunging into it, and spreading it. "Hayyinan" means: slight and easy, not reaching you with any sin.

﴿And it is, in the sight of God, grave﴾, in respect of the burden. This is like his saying (ﷺ) in the hadith of the two graves: "Indeed they are being punished, and they are not being punished for something great", meaning in relation to you.

**Fourteenth:** Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander"? Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it again, if you are believers. And Allah makes the signs clear to you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ This is a rebuke addressed to all the believers. The meaning is: it was incumbent upon you to disapprove of it, and that none of you should take it up and pass it on from one to another by way of relating and transmitting it. You should also have declared Allah exalted above such a thing occurring from the wife of His Prophet, peace be upon him. And you should have judged this statement to be a slander (buhtan). The reality of buhtan is saying about a person what is not in him, whereas ghiba (backbiting) is saying about a person what is in him. This meaning has been reported in the authentic hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Then Allah admonished them against returning to a similar situation. The word "an" (that) is a object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi), with the implied sense of "out of dislike that," or the like.

**Fifteenth:** Allah's words ﴿if you are believers﴾ are a reminder and an emphasis, just as you would say, "It is fitting for you to do such and such, if you are a man."

**Sixteenth:** Allah's words ﴿Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it﴾ refer to Aisha, because "the like of it" can only be a parallel of the accusation concerning the very same person, or concerning one of the same rank as her among the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). This is because such an act harms the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his honour and his family, and that is disbelief (kufr) on the part of the one who does it.

**Seventeenth:** Hisham ibn Ammar said: I heard Malik say, "Whoever insults Abu Bakr and Umar is to be disciplined, and whoever insults Aisha is to be put to death, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it, if you are believers﴾. So whoever insults Aisha has opposed the Qur'an, and whoever opposes the Qur'an is put to death."

Ibn al-Arabi said: The companions of al-Shafi'i said, "Whoever insults Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, is to be disciplined as is done for the rest of the believers. And the words ﴿if you are believers﴾ were not said concerning Aisha, because that [i.e., insulting her] would be disbelief. Rather, it is as he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man does not believe whose neighbour is not safe from his evils.'" And if removing faith in the one who insults Aisha were literal, then removing faith in the statement "An adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer" would also be literal.

We reply: It is not as you claim. Rather, the People of the Slander (ahl al-ifk) accused Aisha, the pure one, of indecency, and Allah cleared her. So everyone who insults her with that of which Allah has cleared her is one who denies Allah, and whoever denies Allah is a disbeliever. This is the path of Malik's position, and it is a clear way for people of insight. And if a man insulted Aisha with something other than that from which Allah cleared her, his punishment would be discipline.

**Eighteenth:** Allah's words ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe﴾: that is, that it should spread and become widely known. It is said: "shā'a al-shay'u shuyū'an, wa-shi'an, wa-shi'ānan, wa-shuyū'uh," meaning it became apparent and spread.

﴿Among those who believe﴾: that is, among the chaste men and the chaste women. By this general expression what is meant is Aisha and Safwan, may Allah be pleased with them both. "Al-fāḥisha" (indecency) is an act that is ugly to an extreme degree. It is also said that "al-fāḥisha" in this verse means an evil statement.

﴿For them is a painful punishment in this world﴾: that is, the prescribed punishment (hadd). ﴿And in the Hereafter, the punishment of the Fire﴾: that is, for the hypocrites, so this is specific. We have already explained that the hadd is an expiation (kaffara) for believers. al-Tabari said: its meaning is, if he dies persisting in it without repenting.

**Nineteenth:** Allah's words ﴿And Allah knows﴾: that is, He knows the magnitude of this sin and the recompense for it, and He knows everything.

﴿And you do not know﴾: it has been narrated from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever supports a man among the people in a dispute about which he has no knowledge, he is in the wrath of Allah until he desists from it. And whoever intercedes on behalf of someone so that a prescribed punishment from the punishments of Allah is not carried out, he has truly defied Allah and brought upon himself His wrath, and the curse of Allah follows him until the Day of Resurrection. And whoever spreads a word against a Muslim man, while he is innocent of it, intending to disgrace him with it in this world, it is incumbent upon Allah to cast him into the Fire with it." Then he recited as its confirmation from the Book of Allah: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe﴾, the verse.

**Twentieth:** Allah's words ﴿O you who have believed, do not follow the steps of Satan﴾: that is, his paths and ways. The meaning: do not travel the road to which Satan calls you. The singular of "khuṭuwāt" is "khuṭwa," which is the distance between the two feet. "Al-khaṭwa" (with a fatḥa) is the verbal noun: one says "khaṭawtu khaṭwatan," and its plural is "khaṭawāt." And "takhaṭṭā ilaynā fulān" (so-and-so stepped over to us), and from this is the hadith that he saw a man stepping over the necks of people on Friday.

The majority of readers recited "khuṭuwāt" with a ḍamma on the ṭā'. ʿĀṣim and al-A'mash read it with sukūn. The majority read "mā zakā" with a light kāf, meaning he was not guided, nor did he accept Islam, nor did he recognise right guidance. It is also said that "mā zakā" means he did not become righteous; one says "zakā yazkū zakā'an," meaning he became righteous. Al-Hasan and Abu Ḥaywa read it with a shaddah, meaning that His purifying you, His cleansing of you and His guidance of you come only through His grace, not through your deeds.

Al-Kisa'i said: "Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū lā tattabiʿū khuṭuwāti al-shayṭān" is a parenthetical clause (mu'taridh), and His words "mā zakā minkum min aḥadin abadan" (none of you would ever have been purified) are the answer to His earlier and second statement: ﴿And if not for the grace of Allah upon you﴾.

**Twenty-first:** Allah's words ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give﴾, the verse. The most well-known of the reports is that this verse was revealed concerning the story of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa, may Allah be pleased with him, and Mistah ibn Uthatha. That was because Mistah was the son of his maternal aunt's daughter, and he was among the poor Emigrants and the Badr veterans. He is Mistah ibn Uthatha ibn ʿAbbad ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manaf. It is also said that his name was Awf, and Mistah was a nickname. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, used to spend on him because of his poverty and kinship. When the matter of the slander occurred, and Mistah said what he said, Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend on him nor benefit him with any benefit ever. Then Mistah came and made excuses, saying: "I was only frequenting the gatherings of Hassan, and I would listen but not speak." Abu Bakr said to him: "You laughed and took part in what was said." And he passed by his right side (i.e., he swore an oath), and then the verse was revealed.

Al-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas said: A group of the believers cut off their benefits from everyone who spoke about the slander, and they said: "By Allah, we will not maintain relations with anyone who spoke about the matter of Aisha." So the verse was revealed concerning all of them.

The first (the report about Abu Bakr and Mistah) is more sound. However, the verse includes the Ummah until the Day of Resurrection, in that no one of virtue and wealth should become angry and swear that he will never benefit one who has such a description.

In the authentic report: when Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you﴾, the ten verses, Abu Bakr, who had been spending on Mistah because of his kinship and poverty, said: "By Allah, I will never spend anything on him again after what he said about Aisha." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give﴾, up to His words: ﴿Do you not like that Allah should forgive you?﴾. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: This is the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah the Exalted. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, I truly love that Allah should forgive me." So he returned to Mistah the provision he used to spend on him and said: "I will never withdraw it from him."

**Twenty-second:** In this verse there is evidence that slander (qadhf), even if it is a major sin, does not nullify good deeds, because Allah the Exalted described Mistah after his statement with emigration and faith. The same applies to all the major sins. Nothing nullifies deeds except associating partners with Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65].

**Twenty-third:** Whoever swears an oath not to do something, then sees that doing it is better, should do it and make expiation (kaffara) for his oath, or make expiation for his oath and then do it, as has preceded in Surat al-Ma'ida. The jurists held that whoever swears never to do a sunnah (a recommended practice) or a mandub (commendable act), and makes that permanent, this is a disqualification (jarh) of his testimony. Al-Baji mentioned this in al-Muntaqa.

**Twenty-fourth:** Allah's words ﴿And let not those of virtue﴾: "wa-lā ya'tali" means he swears, its pattern is yaf'ali, from al-alliyya, which is the oath, and from it is the Exalted's words ﴿for those who swear off from their wives﴾ (al-Baqara: 226), which has already been discussed in Surat al-Baqara. A group said its meaning is "yuqassir" (falls short), from your saying "alawtu fī kadhā" when you fell short in it, and from it is the Exalted's words ﴿they do not fall short in harming you﴾ (Ali 'Imran: 118).

**Twenty-fifth:** Allah's words ﴿Do you not like that Allah should forgive you?﴾ are an illustration and an argument: that is, just as you love Allah's pardon for your sins, so likewise you should forgive those beneath you. To this meaning the Prophet's words, peace be upon him, refer: "He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy."

**Twenty-sixth:** Some scholars said: This is the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah the Exalted, in terms of the gentleness of Allah toward the sinful slanderers through this expression. It was also said: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is His words: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty﴾ [al-Ahzab: 47]. And Allah said in another verse: ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds, in gardens of paradise, for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty﴾ [al-Shura: 22], so this verse explains the great bounty, and the other gives good tidings of it to the believers. Among the verses of hope is His words: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves..."﴾ [al-Zumar: 53], and His words: ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants﴾ [al-Shura: 19]. Some of them said: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha: 5], because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not be content while any one of his Ummah remained in the Fire.

**Twenty-seventh:** Allah's words ﴿that they should give﴾: that is, "an lā yu'tū" (that they should not give), so the "lā" was elided, like the saying of the speaker:

"Fa-qultu yamīnu Allāhi abraḥu qā'idan / wa-law qaṭaʿū ra'sī ladayka wa-awṣālī"

This is the first half of a line of Imru' al-Qays, whose completion is: "Or even if they cut off my head before you and my limbs."

Al-Zajjaj mentioned this. According to the view of Abu Ubayda, there is no need to suppose an elided "lā."

﴿And let them pardon﴾: from "afā al-rab'u," meaning it was effaced, so it is the erasure of the sin, just as the trace of the encampment is effaced.

**Twenty-eight issues** [It should be noted that the issues number twenty-seven in all the originals.]:

**First:** Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you﴾. "*ʿUsbah*" (a group, a band of men bound by mutual support) is the predicate of "*inna*". It is also permissible to put it in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*ḥāl*), in which case the predicate would be: "for every person among them is what he earned of sin."

The cause of its revelation is what the imams narrated from the lengthy *Ḥadīth al-Ifk* (the hadith of the slander, *al-ifk* meaning fabrication or lie) concerning the story of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her. It is a sound and well-known report, whose fame makes its mention unnecessary, and it will come in abridged form. Al-Bukhari transmitted it as a suspended report (*taʿlīq*), and his version is more complete. He said: "And Usamah said, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah." He also transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from his brother Sulayman, from the hadith of Masruq, from Umm Ruman, the mother of ʿĀʾishah, that she said: "When ʿĀʾishah was accused, she fell unconscious."

And from Musa ibn Isma'il, from the hadith of Abu Wa'il, who said: "Masruq ibn al-Ajda' related to me, he said: Umm Ruman, who is the mother of ʿĀʾishah, related to me, she said: While I and ʿĀʾishah were sitting, a woman of the Ansar entered and said: 'May Allah do such-and-such to so-and-so.' Umm Ruman said: 'And what is that?' She said: 'I am among those who spread the story!' She said: 'And what was that?' She said: 'Such-and-such.' ʿĀʾishah said: 'Did he hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' She said: 'Yes.' She said: 'And Abu Bakr?' She said: 'Yes!' So ʿĀʾishah fell unconscious, and she did not recover except with a fever accompanied by shivering [i.e., trembling]. I threw her clothes over her and covered her. The Prophet ﷺ came and said: 'What is the matter with this one?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a fever with shivering has seized her.' He said: 'Perhaps it is because of a report that has been spoken of.' She said: 'Yes.' Then ʿĀʾishah sat up and said: 'By Allah, if I swear an oath, you will not believe me! And if I offer an excuse, you will not accept my excuse! My example and yours is that of Jacob and his sons [i.e., when he said in his trial: "Allah is the One whose help is sought..." and so on], and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.' She said: 'He departed and said nothing, and Allah revealed her innocence.' She said: 'Praise be to Allah, not to anyone's praise, nor to yours.'"

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Humaydi said: "Some of the Baghdadi *ḥuffāẓ* (memorizers of hadith) whom we met used to say: the *irsāl* (a break in the chain) is clearer in this hadith, and they argued for this by the fact that Umm Ruman died during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Masruq did not witness the Prophet ﷺ, without any dispute."

Al-Bukhari also has, from the hadith of ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, that ʿĀʾishah used to recite ﴿when you received it with your tongues﴾ [24:15] and say: "*al-walq* is lying." Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: "She was more knowledgeable than others about that [i.e., about the reading she used], because it was revealed concerning her."

Al-Bukhari said: "Ma'mar [in al-Bukhari it is al-Nuʿmān ibn Rashid] ibn Rashid said, from al-Zuhri: The hadith of the slander occurred in the ghazwah (military campaign) of al-Muraysiʿ." Ibn Ishaq said: "And that was in the year six." Musa ibn ʿUqbah said: "In the year four."

Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: "al-Walid ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said to me: 'Has it reached you that ʿAli was among those who slandered?' I said: 'No, but two men of your people have informed me: Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman and Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, that ʿĀʾishah said to them both: "ʿAli was *musallaman* [silent] regarding her affair."'" [Note: *musallaman*, with a kasra on the *lām* and a shadda, from *tasliym*, meaning silent about her matter. It was also said: with a fatha on the *lām*, from safety from delving into it.]
